package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code is described in this report. The article discusses general supply chain threats and how SLSA and Sonatype products address them, referencing historical incidents (e.g., event-stream, Webmin, Browserify typosquatting, Mimemagic) as examples of attack scenarios. No actual code or package is analyzed.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected modification of build artifacts not matching source repository
Introduction of dependencies with mismatched provenance or source
Typosquatting: package names similar to popular packages but with malicious intent
Sudden unavailability or removal of critical dependencies
Use of untrusted or unofficial package mirrors
file_indicators: Packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting)
Build artifacts with mismatched hashes or provenance records
Dependencies with unknown or unverifiable uploaders
network_indicators: Connections to untrusted or unofficial package mirrors
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages and dependencies whose provenance does not match the expected source repository or builder. Flag and quarantine packages with suspicious or unverifiable uploaders, or those introduced via unofficial mirrors. Detect typosquatting by comparing package names to known popular libraries. Alert on sudden removal or unavailability of critical dependencies. Use behavioral analysis to identify packages exhibiting suspicious installation or runtime behaviors.
